newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Prices firms as sellers backoff.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Prices firms as sellers backoff.

text.p: Singapore middle distillate market firmed on Thursday as sellers pulled back their aggressive offers amid improved sentiment on expectations of fresh demand from China, traders said.
"The market recovered slightly because there are no agressive offers anymore," one trader said.
In the jet fuel market, a 130,000 barrel cargo lifting July was traded at $24.65 per barrel free-on-board (fob), up 45 cents from Wednesday's traded level.
The deal was between a European major and a Singapore trader, sources said.

In addition to the latest trade, industry sources said deals were also done earlier in the week to North Asia with one mid-rage (MR) sized cargo each done to South Korea and China for late July arrival, both ex-Singapore.
The deals were done at about 10 cents premium to spot Singapore quotes on a fob basis.

Traders said jet demand is also picking up from Indonesia which is expected to buy three million for August delivery having already bought a similar amount for July delivery, these are up about one million from its normal monthly import.
Gas oil prices firmed following the absence of aggressive offers which some traders said had led to an artificial deflation of prices.
On Wednesday, a 150,000 barrel cargo traded at a 65 cents per barrel discount to Singapore spot quotes, for July 10-14 lifting, on a fob basis with another done at $22.00 for July 21-25 lifting.
Late Thursday the lowest offer was at $22.50 for Jul 11-15 lifting.

The firmer prices was also reflected in the swaps market where July swaps were quoted at $22.55/$22.65 per barrel, August at $23.00/$23.10, both up about 20 and 25 cents, respectively, from Wednesday, brokers said.
Firmer August prices has also widened the July/August spread to about minus 50 cents from minus 40 cents on Wednesday, they said.
The stronger August prices were attributed to market expectations that demand will pick up by then as Chinese buying returns to normal.
China halved its April imports over March to about 400,000 tonnes with May imports also expected at around this range.
Traders are counting on higher Chinese imports in the third quarter as most feel that the low second quarter imports has lead to lower stocks among Chinese endusers.
Sources also said they expect smuggling actitives to pick up post-handover as the Chinese authorities ease up their current tough crackdown.
Others are also looking towards firmer levels as a correction to the recent large falls as new supply sources such as arbitrage cargoes from the West are closed.
